Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 71, verse 1–4:

Naming of the Surah

• It is named Nuh (Noah), because it mentions the story of Allah's prophet Nuh (peace be upon him), what befell him with his people, and the details of his call and his supplications, from its beginning to its end.

Among the Surah's Objectives

• Mention of Nuh's message and his charge to convey the call, and the use of his people as an example for the polytheists, since they were the first polytheists among the children of Adam. Also the details of his call: commanding the worship of Allah alone and rejecting the worship of idols, reminding of the Day of Resurrection, warning of punishment, and drawing evidence from the wondrous creation of Allah Most High for His sole right to divinity.

[The Tafsir]

Indeed, We sent Nuh to his people, and We said to him: "Warn your people before there comes to them a painful punishment." He said: "O my people, I am a clear warner to you from the punishment of Allah if you disobey Him. Indeed, I am a messenger of Allah to you, so worship Him alone, fear His punishment, and obey me in what I command you and forbid you from. If you obey me and respond to me, Allah will forgive you your sins and grant you forgiveness, and will extend your lives to a term appointed in the knowledge of Allah Most High. Indeed, when death comes, it is never delayed. If only you knew that, you would hasten to faith and obedience."

Noah said: "My Lord, I have called my people to faith in You and obedience to You, by night and by day. But my calling them to faith only made them flee and turn away from it. Indeed, every time I called them to faith in You, so that it might be a cause of Your forgiving their sins, they put their fingers in their ears so as not to hear the call to truth, and covered themselves with their garments so as not to see me. They persisted in their disbelief and were arrogant about accepting faith, with great arrogance. Then I called them to faith openly and publicly, without concealment. Then I made the call known to them in a loud voice at one time, and at another time I spoke to them in a low, quiet voice. And I said to my people: Ask your Lord for the forgiveness of your sins, and turn to Him in repentance from your disbelief. Indeed, He, exalted is He, is ever Forgiving to whoever of His servants repents and returns to Him."

If you repent and seek forgiveness, Allah will send down abundant, continuous rain upon you, increase your wealth and children, make for you gardens whose fruits and beauty you enjoy, and make for you rivers from which you water your crops and your livestock. "What is the matter with you, O people, that you do not fear the greatness and majesty of Allah, when He created you in successive stages: a drop of semen, then a clinging clot, then a lump of flesh, then bones and flesh?" "Have you not considered how Allah created seven heavens, layered one above another, and placed the moon in them as a light, and made the sun a shining lamp by which the people of the earth are illuminated?"

God created your origin from the earth in a creation. Then He will return you into the earth after death, and bring you forth on the Day of Resurrection in a sure bringing forth. And Allah made the earth spread out for you like a carpet, so that you may travel in it along its wide roads.

Noah said: "My Lord, indeed my people have persisted in disobeying me and denying me, and those who are weak among them have followed the chiefs who went astray, whose wealth and children have increased them in nothing but loss in this world and punishment in the Hereafter. And the chiefs of error have plotted against their followers, the weak, with a tremendous plot. And they said to them: 'Do not abandon your gods for the worship of God alone, to which Noah calls you, and do not abandon Wadd, nor Suwa', nor Yaghuth and Ya'uq and Nasr.'" These are the names of their idols which they used to worship besides God. They were the names of righteous men; when they died, Satan inspired their people to set up for them statues and images, so that they would be encouraged—so they claimed—to obey [God] when they saw them. Then, when those people passed away and time lengthened, and others succeeded them, Satan whispered to them that their forefathers used to worship statues and images and seek intercession through them. This is among the wisdoms behind the prohibition of statues and the prohibition of building domes over graves, because with the passage of time they become objects of worship for the ignorant. These chiefs have led many people astray with the paths of deception and error that they made attractive to them. Then Noah, peace be upon him, said: "And do not increase these wrongdoers, O our Lord, who wronged themselves with disbelief and obstinacy, except in destruction." So because of their sins and their persistence in disbelief and transgression, they were drowned by the flood, and immediately after being drowned they were made to enter a great fire of blazing flame and burning, so they found for themselves, besides God, no one to help them or to ward off the punishment of God.

Noah, peace be upon him, said after despairing of his people: "My Lord, do not leave upon the earth any dweller among the disbelievers in You. Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants who have believed, away from the path of truth, and they will beget none but wicked disbelievers in You and disobedient to You. My Lord, forgive me, and my parents, and whoever enters my house as a believer, and the believing men and believing women. And do not increase the wrongdoers except in destruction and loss, in this world and the Hereafter."
